data.title: Lewis Apartments Opens Independence Rental-Home Community Near Downtown Sacramento
data.description:
Lewis Apartments Opens Independence Rental-Home Community Near Downtown Sacramento

Lewis’ Independence in West Sacramento brings 208 brand-new rental homes with private garages and resort-style community amenities to the growing Southport area

Independence in West Sacramento, a new gated community of 208 townhome-style rental homes developed by Lewis Apartments, will officially open its leasing office and model homes to the public on Saturday, October 24. The leasing office and models will be open daily from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261023713030/en/

Lewis Apartments opens Independence multifamily community in West Sacramento

Located in West Sacramento’s Southport/Bridgeway Island area, Independence introduces rental homes designed for residents who want the space and privacy of a single-family home without the responsibilities and costs that homeownership can bring. The community offers brand-new two- and three-bedroom homes ranging from approximately 1,176 to 1,722 square feet, with private entrances, direct-access one- and two-car garages and private outdoor living spaces.

The opening comes as West Sacramento continues to grow as a residential and employment destination directly across the Sacramento River from the urban core. Independence is positioned to serve renters who want to remain closely connected to Downtown and Midtown Sacramento while enjoying more room, convenient parking and a quieter residential setting at home.

Residents have convenient access to Downtown Sacramento, the State Capitol, Golden 1 Center and DOCO, Old Sacramento Waterfront, Sutter Health Park and the region’s major employment and healthcare centers. The community also provides access to I-80, I-5 and Highway 50, connecting residents throughout the greater Sacramento region.

Inside the homes, contemporary features include quartz countertops with full-height backsplashes, stainless-steel ENERGY STAR appliances, induction ranges, French-door refrigerators, modern cabinetry, wood-style plank flooring, in-home washers and dryers, walk-in closets and smart-home technology. Garages include EV-charging capabilities, and select homes provide additional garage storage.

Community amenities include a heated pool and spa with shaded cabanas, a 24-hour fitness center and specialty fitness studio, pickleball courts, outdoor barbecue and gathering areas, a fire table, dog park and dog spa, play area, package lockers and a Borrow-a-Bike program.

Independence in West Sacramento is Lewis’ second Independence rental-home community in Northern California, following Independence in Dixon, which opened in 2025. Building on the momentum of the Dixon and West Sacramento communities, Lewis plans to expand the Independence concept to additional Northern California markets, with future communities planned in Folsom, Vacaville, Fairfield, Newark and other locations.

“The success of Independence in Dixon showed us there is strong demand for rental homes that offer more space, privacy and the features people value in a home, without giving up the flexibility and convenience of renting,” said Randall Lewis of Lewis Group of Companies. “Independence in West Sacramento builds on that success, offering a more residential way of living while keeping residents close to Downtown Sacramento and the region’s major employment centers. It’s an important next step as we expand the Independence concept across Northern California.”

Independence is designed to appeal to a broad range of renters, including Downtown and state-government professionals, healthcare workers, dual-income households, renters relocating to the Sacramento region and residents who may be considering homeownership but prefer the flexibility and convenience of renting.

The community’s location also provides a new alternative for renters considering West Sacramento, Downtown/Midtown Sacramento, Natomas, Davis and other nearby communities. Its combination of a residential setting and central regional access supports the community’s positioning: “Close to Downtown. More room to live.”

The Independence in West Sacramento leasing office and model homes are located at 3350 Freedom Lane, West Sacramento, CA 95691. Beginning October 24, they will be open daily from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.

For leasing information, floor plans and current availability, visit Independence in West Sacramento, CA | Welcome Home.

About Lewis Group of Companies

Established in 1955, the Lewis Group of Companies is one of the nation’s largest privately held community developers, with a legacy that includes more than 58,000 homes, 13,000 apartments and 24 million square feet of retail, office and industrial space throughout California and Nevada.

Lewis has proudly served the Sacramento region since 1975, developing communities designed to enhance the way people live and work. Over the past five decades, Lewis has built more than 15,000 homes, developed three shopping centers and completed more than 2,500 multifamily units throughout Northern California, with a robust pipeline of residential and mixed-use development planned across the region. Learn more at lewisgroupofcompanies.com.

data.title: Some Republicans are opposing Trump on tariffs. Maine's Susan Collins just got him to back down on Canadian levies.
data.description:
By Victor Reklaitis

As she faces a tough midterm race, the five-term GOP senator is touting her successful lobbying effort against certain tariffs on Canada

One closely watched race in this fall's midterm elections is the U.S. Senate race in Maine between Republican incumbent Susan Collins and Democratic challenger Troy Jackson.

Republican Sen. Susan Collins, who is in a tight re-election fight in Maine, announced Friday that nine categories of products crucial for her state's agricultural industries will be exempted from President Donald Trump's tariffs on Canada, saying the shift comes after she repeatedly lobbied Trump administration officials.

The move by Collins is a fresh sign of how some Republican candidates are showing a willingness to oppose Trump on certain tariffs, even as import taxes are among his favorite policy tools.

The GOP's Senate nominee in Michigan, former Rep. Mike Rogers, has released an ad in which he says: "Here in Michigan, we know that Canada is not our enemy. We need to end this tariff war now." Rogers is in a similarly tight race, facing off against Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed, a former local health official.

In New Hampshire's Senate race, Republican nominee John Sununu has said it "doesn't make any sense to engage in a trade war with Canada." Sununu's midterm contest against Democratic nominee Chris Pappas, a congressman, is rated as "leans Democratic" by the nonpartisan Cook Political Report, while the races in Maine and Michigan are rated as "toss-ups."

The GOP candidates who question Trump's tariffs appear to be putting themselves in alignment with most voters. An AP-NORC poll in September found that 64% of U.S. adults think Trump has gone too far in imposing new tariffs on other countries, up from 58% in January.

The challenge for these Republican politicians is they have to address the widespread view that tariffs lead to higher prices, but "there are certain sectors where these tariffs could be strategically popular," said Nathan Dean, a senior government analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence. "And so they have to balance that line."

Dean told MarketWatch that the GOP candidates need to distance themselves from the president "enough for the election," but not so much that they're "out of step with him next year," when tariffs look likely to ramp back up.

In a statement on Friday, Collins noted that she previously secured tariff exemptions for other Canadian products that are crucial for Mainers - namely road salt, cement and wood pulp - and promised to "continue working directly with administration officials to seek additional relief from tariffs and encourage a broader trade agreement with Canada, our neighbor, ally and largest trading partner." The five-term senator said the categories of products receiving exemptions include corrugated paper cartons, plastic boxes, plastic bags, refrigeration and freezing equipment, packing and wrapping machinery, and seaweed and algae products.

Her Democratic opponent, Troy Jackson, criticized Collins over her announcement.

"Trump's trade wars have made life harder and more expensive for Mainers. Susan Collins enabled this chaos, voted to confirm the people behind it, and now wants credit for bringing a cup of water to put out the fire," said Jackson, a former state legislator, in a social-media post.

"We deserve a senator who stands up to Trump - not one who rubber-stamps his agenda and begs for relief from the chaos she helped create," he added.

The White House didn't immediately respond to MarketWatch's request for comment on Collins's announcement. The tariff reductions that Collins is celebrating may be balanced out by raising levies on other Canadian goods, according to a Wall Street Journal report.

Trump's trade fight with Canada went to a new level in August after negotiations on a trade deal broke down, and it escalated further in September with Trump's bans on Canadian dairy products, some alcoholic beverages and other goods.

-Victor Reklaitis

data.title: Summit Therapeutics and Lunit Announce Agreement to Apply AI-powered SCOPE IO Platform for Tumor Microenvironment Analysis in Immuno-Oncology Development
data.description:
Summit Therapeutics and Lunit Announce Agreement to Apply AI-powered SCOPE IO Platform for Tumor Microenvironment Analysis in Immuno-Oncology Development

Research Will Use Lunit’s AI-powered Pathology Platform to Analyze H&E Whole-Slide Images and Generate Scalable Insights into Tumor Microenvironment Biology

Summit Therapeutics Inc. (NASDAQ: SMMT) and Lunit Inc. (KRX: 328130) today announced a research agreement to evaluate the use of Lunit SCOPE IO, Lunit’s AI-powered pathology platform, for tumor microenvironment analysis in support of Summit’s immuno-oncology development programs with ivonescimab.

The effort will focus on applying Lunit SCOPE IO to hematoxylin and eosin-stained (H&E) whole-slide images to characterize tumor microenvironment features. The companies aim to explore how AI-powered pathology analysis can support biomarker discovery, patient stratification or selection, and a deeper biological understanding of response to ivonescimab therapies.

Summit is developing ivonescimab, a novel, potential first-in-class investigational PD-1 / VEGF bispecific antibody, in several solid tumors. Lunit SCOPE IO is designed to support immuno-oncology research and biomarker development through AI-powered analysis of H&E slides, enabling scalable assessment of tumor microenvironment features without requiring additional stains or assays.

“Understanding the tumor microenvironment is increasingly important as immuno-oncology moves beyond single-axis checkpoint inhibition toward more complex mechanisms and combinations,” said Allen Yang, MD, PhD, Chief Research and Development Strategy Officer of Summit. “We are pleased to work with Lunit to explore how AI-powered pathology can help generate deeper, more scalable insights from routine tissue samples and inform the continued development of ivonescimab.”

“Summit is at the forefront of next-generation immuno-oncology development, and we are excited to support its efforts with Lunit SCOPE IO,” said Brandon Suh, Lunit CEO. “By extracting quantitative, spatially resolved immune and tumor microenvironment features from standard H&E slides, we believe SCOPE IO can help biopharma partners better understand which patients may benefit from immuno-oncology therapies and why.”

This agreement reflects the growing importance of computational pathology in oncology drug development. Routine H&E slides contain rich information about tumor architecture, immune infiltration, stromal organization, and spatial interactions within the tumor microenvironment. However, traditional manual assessment can be difficult to scale and may not fully capture the quantitative and spatial complexity of the tumor-immune interface. AI-powered analysis offers the potential to convert these routinely generated pathology images into reproducible, high-dimensional biomarker data.

The companies expect the work to generate tumor microenvironment insights that may inform future translational research, exploratory biomarker strategies, and clinical development planning. No clinical outcome data are being announced as part of this release.

Lunit SCOPE products are for research use only. Not for use in diagnostic procedures or decisions.

About Ivonescimab

Ivonescimab, known as SMT112 in Summit’s license territories, North America, South America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Japan, and as AK112 outside of Summit’s license territories, is a novel, potential first-in-class investigational bispecific antibody combining the effects of immunotherapy via a blockade of PD-1 with the anti-angiogenesis effects associated with blocking VEGF into a single molecule. By design, ivonescimab displays unique cooperative binding to each of its intended targets with multifold higher affinity to PD-1 when in the presence of VEGF.

This design is intended to differentiate ivonescimab as there is potentially higher expression (presence) of both PD-1 and VEGF in tumor tissue and the tumor microenvironment (TME) as compared to normal tissue in the body. Summit believes ivonescimab’s specifically engineered tetravalent structure (four binding sites) enables higher avidity (accumulated strength of multiple binding interactions) in the TME (Zhong, et al, iScience, 2025). This tetravalent structure, the intentional novel design of the molecule, and bringing these two targets into a single bispecific antibody with cooperative binding qualities have the potential to direct ivonescimab to the tumor tissue versus healthy tissue. The intent of ivonescimab’s design, together with a half-life of 6 to 7 days after the first dose (Zhong, et al, iScience, 2025) increasing to approximately 10 days at steady state dosing, is to improve upon previously established efficacy thresholds, side effects, and safety profiles associated with prior approved drugs to these targets.

Ivonescimab was invented by Akeso Inc. (HKEX Code: 9926.HK) and is currently utilized in multiple Phase III clinical trials. Over 5,000 patients have been treated with ivonescimab in clinical studies globally and over 100,000 patients when considering those treated in a commercial setting in China, as noted by Akeso.

There are currently 17 Phase III clinical studies that are either announced, ongoing, or have been completed studying ivonescimab, five of which are Summit-sponsored global studies, two of which are studies sponsored by cooperative groups, and 10 of which are being or have been conducted in China by Akeso. Summit began its clinical development of ivonescimab in NSCLC (HARMONi, HARMONi-3, HARMONi-7) and expanded its sponsored Phase III clinical development program into colorectal cancer (CRC; HARMONi-GI3) and urothelial carcinoma (bladder cancer; HARMONi-GU1). The two cooperative studies are in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC; ILLUMINE) and biliary tract cancer (BTC; EA2251).

Five Phase III ivonescimab clinical trials have read out to date, all five with positive data. Four of these five studies are in NSCLC and one is in BTC. In addition to Summit’s positive HARMONi study in NSCLC, Akeso has had positive read-outs in four single-region (China), randomized Phase III clinical trials, HARMONi-A, HARMONi-2, HARMONi-6 (each in NSCLC), and HARMONi-GI1 (in BTC) for ivonescimab, including a statistically significant overall survival benefit in all four studies from China.

Akeso is actively conducting additional Phase III clinical studies in settings outside of NSCLC and biliary-tract cancer, including triple-negative breast cancer, head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, small cell lung cancer, colorectal cancer, and pancreatic cancer.

Ivonescimab is an investigational therapy that is not approved by any regulatory authority in Summit’s license territories, including the United States and Europe. Ivonescimab was initially approved for marketing authorization in China in May 2024.

About Lunit Inc.

Founded in 2013, Lunit (KRX: 328130) is a global leader on a mission to conquer cancer through AI. Our clinically validated solutions span medical imaging, breast health, and biomarker analysis, empowering earlier detection, smarter treatment decisions, and more precise outcomes across the cancer care continuum.

Lunit offers a comprehensive suite spanning risk prediction and early detection to precision oncology. Our FDA-cleared Lunit INSIGHT Breast Suite and breast health solutions support cancer screening in thousands of medical institutions worldwide, while the Lunit SCOPE platform is used in research partnership with global pharma and laboratory leaders for biomarker research, and companion diagnostic development.

Trusted by over 10,000 sites in more than 65 countries, Lunit combines deep medical expertise with continuously evolving datasets to deliver measurable impact for patients, clinicians, and researchers alike. Headquartered in Seoul with global offices, Lunit is driving the worldwide fight against cancer. Learn more at lunit.io.

About Summit Therapeutics Inc.

Summit Therapeutics Inc. is a biopharmaceutical oncology company focused on the discovery, development, and commercialization of patient-, physician-, caregiver- and societal-friendly medicinal therapies intended to improve quality of life, increase potential duration of life, and resolve serious unmet medical needs.

Summit was founded in 2003 and the company’s shares are listed on the Nasdaq Global Market (symbol "SMMT"). Summit is headquartered in Miami, Florida, with additional offices in Palo Alto, California, Princeton, New Jersey, Dublin, Ireland, and Oxford, UK.

For more information, please visit https://www.smmttx.com and follow Summit on X @SMMT_TX.

data.title: The U.S. economy is great by this measure, and the good times aren't over. So why are Americans so sour?
data.description:
By Jeffry Bartash

A once-in-a-generation investment boom has created lots of winners - but many Americans are feeling left out

The U.S. economy heated up even as the weather cooled. Can the good times keep going?

An unyielding U.S. economy has shrugged off a number of blows to keep growing at a faster-than-expected speed - and there's a good chance the six-year old expansion has a lot more room to run.

The economy is poised to show a growth rate of 3% or more from July to September when the government next week reports gross domestic product for the third quarter. The U.S. might even be on track to post frothy annual growth of 2.5% in 2026.

It wasn't supposed to happen.

Many economists predicted growth would slow after the spring as spending from large tax refunds dried up and the U.S.-hosted World Cup ended. High oil prices (CL00) (BRN00), rising inflation, the lingering effect of tariffs and the ongoing conflict with Iran were expected depress growth.

Instead, consumer spending picked up and businesses boosted investment.

The economy still faces lots of challenges, no doubt. The latest obstacle is rising interest rates as the Federal Reserve tries to bring inflation under control. Higher interest rates could even threaten a stock-market boom DJIA SPX COMP that's given the economy a huge dose of adrenalin.

Yet the good times could also go on for quite a while, spearheaded by a once-in-a-generation investment boom in new technologies such as artificial intelligence.

The investment boom has supercharged the economy by raising productivity, hoisting profits, driving record stock-market gains and underpinning consumer spending, especially among the wealthy.

And yet, most Americans aren't feeling the burn.

High inflation is the biggest killjoy - goods and services cost about 30% more now than they did before the COVID-19 pandemic. Wages are barely keeping up with inflation, if that. And people worry about AI taking their jobs, raising their energy bills or worse.

"If most people ask, 'Am I better off now than I was four years ago,' the answer is, 'Not really,'"said Jim Baird, chief investment officer of Plante Moran Financial Advisors in Michigan.

Faster track

Just a few years ago, the fastest rate of growth the economy was thought to be able to sustain each year was around 1.8%, a mediocre number historically.

And now? Many economists think the U.S. can grow 2% to 2.5% a year through the rest of the decade, barring an unforeseen shock.

The early returns look good. GDP grew at an average annual clip of 2.7% from 2022 to 2025. Massive government stimulus helped for the few years after the pandemic, but consumers and businesses have carried the load the past two years.

The secret sauce of the economy has been an explosion in business investment.

First, companies spent on software and other technologies to improve production at a time of yawning labor shortages. Then, the piled money into AI as machine learning promised to open the door to an even more profitable future.

All the spending seems to have worked. The productivity of workers and businesses - the key to a higher standard of living - has accelerated since the pandemic.

From 2022 to 2025, for instance, productivity rose by an average annual rate of 2.4%, compared to a 1.4% rate in the five years before the 2020 onset of the pandemic. Similar increases are likely in the next five years if AI actually delivers.

"The AI revolution is real," said Eugenio Aleman, chief economist at Raymond James. "This is not your father's housing bubble."

Rising productivity simply means each worker can do more in the same amount of time as they did in the year before. Steadily rising productivity allows companies to earn high profits and even pay their workers more.

Profits have definitely risen, in many cases allowing businesses to cope with higher oil prices and inflation.

Profit margins - how much a company earns per every $100 in sales - have reached historic highs in the past few years. Margins for S&P 500 companies reached almost 16% this year, compared to 8% to 12% a year from 2010 to 2019.

For a while, workers also reaped the benefits in the form of higher wages and benefits. Annual increases in compensation jumped to as high as 5% in 2022 - almost double the prepandemic trend - when companies were scrambling to hire people at a time of acute labor shortages.

No longer is that the case. Wages and benefits are now rising a little over 3% a year, but that's not enough to keep up with inflation. The result: Millions of Americans are falling behind financially, at least for now.

Wealth effect

The news is not all bad. Strong GDP may mask the hardships many Americans face, but a steadily growing economy also means most jobs are not in danger. Layoffs are near a historic low and unemployment is also unusually low.

Good job security, in turn, gives Americans the comfort to keep spending at levels sufficient to propel the economy forward. And that's what they have been doing.

Consumer spending, which accounts for two-thirds of economic growth, has risen by a healthy 2.6% a quarter since 2022, government data show.

A close look at where all the spending is coming from, however, also reveals fractures in the economy that a broad statistic like GDP cannot.

A highly publicized study last year by Moody's Analytics contended the richest 10% of Americans earning $250,000 a year or more accounted for a record 50% of all consumer spending.

The estimate has been much debated, but economists all agree: The wealthy are definitely in the driver's seat of the U.S. economy. It's not so great, as Baird put it, for working-class or lower-income Americans living paycheck to paycheck.

AI plays a big role this, too. The stock market has skyrocketed since the pandemic largely because of massive gains in companies like Nvidia (NVDA) that are at the center of the AI revolution.

All the wealth produced by the stock market has enabled older Americans to splurge on themselves and their kids. Economists call it the "wealth effect."

"It's been an incredibly powerful driver of spending over the last several years," said Michael Pearce, chief U.S. economist at Oxford Economics.

The AI revolution probably has a lot more room to run, too. As companies better figure out how to use AI, productivity could continue to surge at least until the end of the decade. Profits are likely to stay high and perhaps push the stock market higher.

"I think we are still in the very early innings in learning how to deploy AI effectively," Baird said.

Labor's role

The economy is going to need it, especially with a slower-growing or even declining labor force.

The growth rate of any economy - and worker pay, too - is determined in the long run by the combination of population growth and productivity growth. If the population is flat, the economy can only grow by workers and businesses becoming more productive.

From 1950 to 2025, the size of the potential labor force rose about 1.4% a year, according to government data. The labor force is expected to rise an average of just 0.4% a year or less through 2030, the nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office estimates.

The labor force could even shrink if more baby boomers retire soon and the Trump administration's freeze on immigration persists.

That's why the performance of the U.S. economy - and even the American way of life - might become more dependent on higher productivity in the age of AI. It's the only way chronic labor shortages will be alleviated and bigger wage gains for workers are likely to be realized.

"It means the economy is more dependent on productivity gains," Pearce at Oxford Economics said. "If they were disappointing, the economy could slow more sharply."

Whatever the case, the only way most Americans are likely to appreciate strong GDP reports are if they can feel the actual benefits of a steadily growing economy in their own lives -mainly through rising real wages, lower inflation and lots of available jobs. None of those conditions exist right now.

"The economy is growing, but it's not translating into higher income growth and employment," Aleman at Raymond James said.

-Jeffry Bartash

data.title: Stockholders of Sunrise Realty Trust, a Tannenbaum Capital Group Affiliate, Approve Merger-Related Proposal with Southern Realty Trust; Company Declares Stub Period Dividend
data.description:
WEST PALM BEACH, Fla., Oct. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Sunrise Realty Trust, Inc. (Nasdaq: SUNS) (“SUNS” or the “Company”), a lender on the Tannenbaum Capital Group (“TCG”) Real Estate platform, today announced that its stockholders approved the issuance of approximately 8,464,955 shares of SUNS common stock, subject to certain adjustments, in connection with the Company’s previously announced merger with Southern Realty Trust Inc. (“SRT”) (the “Merger”) at the Company’s special meeting of stockholders held earlier today (the “Special Meeting”). Approximately 59.5% of the outstanding shares of SUNS common stock were voted virtually or by proxy at the Special Meeting, and approximately 91.6% of the votes cast at the Special Meeting were voted in favor of the proposal. SRT stockholders also approved the Merger at its special meeting held earlier today. The approvals represent a key milestone toward combining SUNS and SRT into a larger, more efficient Nasdaq-listed commercial real estate lending platform.

“We appreciate the support of our stockholders as we advance this strategic combination,” said Leonard M. Tannenbaum, Executive Chairman. “The Merger is expected to create a larger, more efficient lending platform with increased scale and improved access to capital, positioning us to continue to generate attractive risk-adjusted returns and build long-term stockholder value. We look forward to completing the Merger and welcoming SRT stockholders to SUNS.”

Final voting results from the Special Meeting will be disclosed in a Current Report on Form 8-K to be filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”).

Pursuant to the Agreement and Plan of Merger relating to the Merger (the “Merger Agreement”), SUNS’ Board of Directors declared a prorated cash dividend of $0.09 per share of SUNS common stock (the “Stub Period Dividend”) for the fourth quarter through the day prior to the closing of the Merger. The Stub Period Dividend is payable on November 5, 2026 to the stockholders of record on November 2, 2026.

The Merger is expected to close on November 5, 2026, subject to the satisfaction of remaining customary closing conditions. Upon closing, SRT will merge with and into a wholly owned subsidiary of SUNS, and SUNS common stock will continue to trade on Nasdaq under the symbol “SUNS.”

About Sunrise Realty Trust, Inc.

Sunrise Realty Trust, Inc. (Nasdaq: SUNS) (“SUNS” or the “Company”) is an institutional commercial real estate (“CRE”) lender providing flexible financing solutions to sponsors of CRE projects located primarily in the Southern United States. It focuses on transitional CRE business plans with the potential for near-term value creation, collateralized by top-tier assets predominantly located in established and rapidly expanding Southern markets. For additional information regarding the Company, please visit www.sunriserealtytrust.com.

About TCG Real Estate

TCG Real Estate refers to a group of affiliated CRE-focused debt vehicles, including a Nasdaq-listed mortgage real estate investment trust (“REIT”), Sunrise Realty Trust, Inc. (Nasdaq: SUNS), and a private mortgage REIT, Southern Realty Trust Inc. The vehicles provide flexible financing on transitional CRE properties that present opportunities for near-term value creation, with a focus on top-tier CRE assets located primarily within markets in the Southern U.S. benefiting from economic tailwinds with growth potential. For additional information regarding TCG Real Estate, please visit www.theTCG.com.

data.title: Archer to Launch Air Taxis in Texas — Update
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton 




  Archer Aviation plans to launch air taxi networks in three Texas cities. 



  The electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft are slated to be used for air-taxi services in Austin, Houston and the Dallas-Fort Worth area, the aircraft company said Friday. 



  Archer still requires approval from the Federal Aviation Administration for its air taxi aircraft Midnight. It is in the final stages of that regulatory process. 



  The company plans to begin demo flights in Texas next year. The networks created in the three Texan cities are meant to allow it to scale commercial operations following approval. 



  The goal of the planned launches is to increase connectivity between major airports, business hubs and tourist destinations. Archer cited the Texas cities' high traffic volume as a potential benefit of the fleets. 



  The expansion comes after Boeing agreed to take a nearly 20% stake in Archer. The deal, agreed upon in August, is set to give Archer control of Boeing's flying-taxi venture Wisk Aero, its air-traffic software provider SkyGrid and its drone maker Insitu. 



  Archer, a California-based startup, recently completed the Northern California leg of its flight tour, which was meant to show how air taxis would work in urban areas. The tour flew into seven cities over a three-day period. 





  Write to Katherine Hamilton at katherine.hamilton@wsj.com
